title: Embeddings: Meaning as Geometry
summary: A model cannot do arithmetic on a token ID, so the first thing it does is swap each ID for a learned vector. Similar meanings end up pointing in similar directions, and that geometry is what the rest of the network, and every semantic search system, builds on.
objectives: Explain an embedding table as a learned lookup from token ID to vector and count its parameters
Compute a dot product and a cosine similarity by hand and say when each is appropriate
Explain why vector arithmetic such as king − man + woman lands near queen, and where the idea breaks
Distinguish static token embeddings from contextual embeddings produced deeper in the network
Estimate the storage and compute cost of an embedding index
prerequisites: You should know how text becomes token IDs ([Tokenization](/learn/model-foundations/tokenization)) and how a network is trained by gradient descent ([How a Network Learns](/learn/model-foundations/how-networks-learn)). Vectors are introduced from scratch.
